study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Di Biase et al., Molecular Psychiatry, 2022
study_identification_part.si4_title: Cell type-specific manifestations of cortical thickness heterogeneity in schizophrenia

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To determine whether individual cortical thickness (CTh) heterogeneity in schizophrenia aligns with interregional variation in neural cell-type gene expression and to validate cell-based subtypes using person-specific genetic risk (PRS).

rci1_dataset_name.answer: Human Connectome Project-Young Adult Sample; HCP Early Psychosis; Australian Schizophrenia Research Bank (ASRB)
rci1_dataset_name.reason: The 'Datasets' section explicitly lists the three independent datasets used in the study for both the discovery (HCP) and validation (ASRB) cohorts.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: This study comprised a total of 1849 participants drawn from three independent datasets: (1) the Human Connectome Project-Young Adult Sample [15]; (2) the Human Connectome Project for Early Psychosis (HCPpsychosis) [16]; and (3) the Australian Schizophrenia Research Bank (ASRB) [17].

rci2_hc_n.reason: Healthy control sample sizes are explicitly stated for both discovery and validation cohorts. Discovery cohort (HCP-Young Adult + HCP-Psychosis) had 1127 controls, and validation cohort (ASRB) had 185 controls.
rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: The HCP-Young Adult Sample and HCP-psychosis datasets were acquired using very similar MRI protocols (see Supplementary Material), enabling them to be combined to form a single discovery cohort (n = 1267 comprising 140 cases [age: 22.78 ± 3.83; 48(34%) females] and 1127 controls [age: 28.50 ± 3.83); 598(53%) females]. The ASRB dataset was used to evaluate replicability and validity (n = 520 comprising 335 cases [age: 39.70 ± 10.81; 100(30%) females] and 185 controls [age: 41.05 ± 14.02); 94(51%) females].

rci5_imaging_modality.reason: T1-weighted MRI is clearly stated as the imaging modality used across all three datasets with specific acquisition parameters provided.
rci5_imaging_modality.supporting_text: Acquisition. T1-weighted brain MRI scans were acquired as follows: HCP-1200 (3T Connectome Siemens Skyra: Voxel resolution=.7mm3, TR=2400ms, TE=2.14ms); HCP-Psychosis (Siemens MAGNETOM Prisma 3T: Voxel resolution=.8mm3, TR=2400ms, TE=2.22ms); and ASRB (Siemens Avanto 1.5T: Voxel resolution=1mm3, TR=1980ms, TE=4.3ms).

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.answer: FreeSurfer v5.3 (HCP datasets); FreeSurfer v6.0 (ASRB); Desikan-Killiany parcellation
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The preprocessing pipeline is clearly described with specific FreeSurfer versions for each dataset. Standard FreeSurfer processing steps are detailed including intensity normalization, nonbrain tissue removal, spatial normalization, segmentation, and surface reconstruction. The Desikan-Killiany atlas was used for parcellation.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: T1-weighted images comprising the ASRB dataset were processed using FreeSurfer version 6 [4]. Processing and CTh estimation for the HCP-psychosis dataset followed the HCP1200 pipeline to facilitate harmonization of the HCP datasets. In brief, T1-weighted images for these datasets were processed using FreeSurfer version 5.3 [4]. For all three datasets, preprocessing included intensity normalization, nonbrain tissue removal and spatial normalization to Talairach-like space. Preprocessed images were segmented into gray matter, white matter and cerebrospinal fluid, after which white matter and gray matter surfaces were reconstructed. CTh was estimated for each surface vertex based on the distance separating the gray and white matter surfaces and averaged over all vertices comprising each of the 68 cortical regions (34 per hemisphere) of the Desikan-Killiany atlas [5, 6].

rci8_quality_checking.detail: HCP-psychosis: Visual QC following ENIGMA protocols with medial/lateral snapshots inspection; all images satisfied reconstruction criteria (all lobes present, label positions normal). HCP-1200: Excluded n=151 subjects with documented brain anatomical, processing or noise issues based on 'QC_Issue' variable.
rci8_quality_checking.supporting_text: Quality control. For the HCP-psychosis cohort, where quality control was not previously performed, raw data were checked for anatomical, processing and noise issues. Furthermore, FreeSufer quality control was performed as per ENIGMA protocols http://enigma.ini.usc.edu/protocols/imaging-protocols/, which generates medial and lateral snapshots for visual inspection of FreeSurfer reconstructions. All images satisfied reconstruction criteria (i.e., all lobes were present and label positions did not differ from the general case). For the HCP-1200 cohort, subjects with documented brain anatomical, processing or noise issues (n=151) based on the HCP supplied 'QC_Issue' variable were excluded from the current analyses.

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: ComBat by site/scanner (HCP: 4 sites; ASRB: 5 sites); ANCOVA confirmed removal of scanner differences
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: For HCP (discovery), each measure was harmonized across 4 sites ... For ASRB (validation), each measure was harmonized across 5 sites ... Harmonization successfully removed all scanner differences (see Supplementary Figure 1).

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: CTh heterogeneity in schizophrenia aligns with cell-type gene expression patterns, enabling biologically informed subtyping that is supported by subtype-specific genetic risk associations.
